requirements.text: A single fast check (`hawiyya check`) runs lint, types, import contracts, unit tests and traceability.
Layer dependencies point downward only, enforced by an import contract.
Independence contract: G2 imports nothing from L2, G1 or ported Tahdeed code.
Label isolation contract: L2 to L5 import only the registration view.
Every MUST requirement in a completed phase is named by at least one test.
Every claims register pointer resolves.
No em dash appears in any tracked text file.
No institutional affiliation is mentioned and no real authority is named outside docs/CONTEXT.md.
Same inputs and seed give byte identical outputs.
The logging helper refuses values that could carry a name or an identifier.
Every number in a rendered document matches its source file in results/.
Generated documents (traceability matrix, claims register) are fresh.
Every contract model round trips through JSON.
Generated JSON Schema, TypeScript types and the bilingual field dictionary are fresh.
A Record containing a truth label field is rejected.
A Decision without an evidence object is rejected.
Identifier kinds, capture methods and reason codes are enums; each reason code has English and Arabic descriptions.
Conventions hold: probabilities in [0, 1], dates carry a precision flag, timestamps are UTC.
The same seed gives an identical registry.
Every injected duplicate has ground truth.
The registration view never contains a truth field.
The lexicon excludes every denylisted family name and the generator never produces a denylisted name combination.
The population adapter fails loudly, naming the file and column, when the CSV schema drifts.
Hashes in data/MANIFEST.json verify.
The data source field in the manifest matches the README and data statement.
Hard negatives are present: twins, siblings, same name father and son, cousins, coincidental date of birth and sex, newborn sharing the mother's identifier, unrelated people sharing a placeholder.
At least six synthetic facilities, each with a registration style.
The skeleton collision rate of the lexicon is measured and written to results/lexicon_report.json.
Synthetic identifiers follow the documented format (15 digits, prefix 784, birth year segment) and placeholders are generated.
Tier S (5,000 persons) and Tier M (20,000 persons) are generated.
Tier L (100,000 persons) is generated.
An optional documented age and sex re weighting, labelled ASSUMPTION.
Ported Arabic and Latin normalisation (diacritics, tatweel, alef, ya, digits, accents).
Consonant skeleton, coarse key and Arabizi digit decoding.
Person name model: prefixes, glued prefixes, compound given names, abbreviations, initials, honorifics, single token names.
Date normalisation with precision flags and transposition variants.
Identifier normalisation and identifier kind classification.
Pattern based placeholder detection for identifiers and dates.
Data driven placeholder detection with precision and recall reported against injected truth.
Term frequency tables built from the registry itself.
Normalisation is idempotent (property test).
A golden table of at least 40 name variants matches the expected keys.
No function in L2 reads a truth field.
A vowel aware whole name similarity used as an extra comparison level.
Script detection (Arabic, Latin, Arabizi, mixed).
Multi pass blocking with a union of candidate pairs.
Placeholder identifiers never produce blocking keys.
A cap per block with a sorted neighbourhood fallback; pair completeness lost to the cap is reported.
Discrete comparison levels for names, date of birth, sex, identifier, phone, nationality and area.
Comparison levels are symmetric in record order.
Missing data never turns a hard field disagreement into agreement.
Blocking metrics: pair completeness, reduction ratio, candidate pairs per record.
Identifier capture method modifies identifier level reliability.
Score is prior log odds plus the sum of per level log likelihood ratios; a hand worked example matches to six decimals.
Unsupervised EM estimation with informed initialisation.
Label fitted parameters as an upper bound, with the EM gap reported.
Term frequency adjustment for names, dates of birth and phone suffixes.
A level involving a placeholder contributes exactly zero.
Isotonic calibration fitted on family grouped development data, with ECE and an interval per probability.
Scores are symmetric in record order.
Adding an agreeing field never lowers the score; adding a hard conflict never raises it.
Evidence items sum to the log odds.
The scorer never receives a truth field.
A supervised gradient boosted reference on the same comparison levels.
Vectorised scoring throughput is measured against the budget of 200,000 pairs per second.
Cost based decision with closed form thresholds.
A higher calibrated probability never gives a less permissive decision.
Raising the false merge cost never increases the number of LINK decisions.
Raising the review cost never increases the number of REVIEW decisions.
HARD_CONFLICT guard: distinct reader captured identifiers of the same kind cannot LINK.
POSSIBLE_TWIN_OR_SIBLING guard: never LINK on name and date alone.
POSSIBLE_PARENT_CHILD_SHARED_ID guard: never LINK.
PLACEHOLDER_ONLY, COMMON_NAME_ONLY and DOB_PLACEHOLDER_SUSPECTED cap the decision at REVIEW.
Clustering never merges a contradicted pair silently (CLUSTER_CONFLICT).
Three sentence explanations in English and Arabic rendered from the evidence object.
Next best question by value of information, never negative, only form fields.
A decision is reproducible from its stored inputs hash.
Fail closed: no LINK without a complete evidence table.
Review queue state machine allows only legal transitions.
The audit log hash chain verifies and detects a tampered line.
The audit log contains no name or identifier from the registry.
A registration check on a record that exists exactly returns it first.
FHIR R4 style Patient bundle export with Patient.link validates against the project schema and carries the synthetic statement.
CSV of review cases and a one page summary, each with the synthetic statement.
Simulated reviewer with configurable accuracy and time per case.
Review priority by expected cost and age.
Fail open for registration: an internal failure returns an empty advisory result, never blocks registration.
G2 independent generator with its own variant tables and heavier noise.
Baselines B0 to B5 run on the same pairs as the product.
Metrics: pairwise precision, recall, F1, false merges per 10,000 records, B cubed, review rate, risk coverage, ECE.
Stratification by name origin group and script pair with counts and 95 percent intervals; strata add up to totals.
A gold set of at least 80 pairs used as a smoke test.
Sealed seeds are touched only by `hawiyya eval --sealed`; the run is recorded in results/SEALED_RUN.json.
Decision policies used by the lab are pure functions.
The name origin label is provably not a model input.
Experiments E1 to E9 write results/*.json.
Predictions were committed before the first experiment result and each is marked hit or miss.
Health, registry summary, registration check and name analysis endpoints.
Every listed endpoint exists under /v1 and has an API test.
Errors use application/problem+json.
Bounded inputs and a request size limit.
Static mode: `hawiyya snapshot` writes every response the console needs.
A browser side scorer for the registration check in static mode.
Server logs contain no names or identifiers.
The synthetic data banner is on every screen and cannot be dismissed.
All ten console screens exist with loading, empty and error states.
English and Arabic with right to left layout.
Every name is rendered inside a bidi isolating element.
Text contrast meets WCAG 2.2 AA and graphical objects 3:1, checked by a test.
Automated accessibility checks (axe) pass on every screen.
Every chart has a table alternative and shows intervals.
Dark theme.
LINK, REVIEW and KEEP_APART are encoded by shape and label as well as colour.
Registration check controls have touch targets of at least 44 pixels.
Audit log screen with hash chain status.
